  children={"Enqueue a work unit onto a process path's work pool"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/paths/{pathId}/work-units"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>

:::caution[deprecated]

This endpoint has been deprecated and may be replaced or removed in future versions of the API.

:::

Adds a releasable unit of work (e.g. a pick task) to a process path's `WorkPool` — the EnqueueWorkUnit use case. `workUnitId` is client-supplied and must be unique within the pool: enqueueing the same `workUnitId` twice returns `409 Conflict` (`work-unit-already-enqueued`) rather than silently creating a duplicate entry — this endpoint is idempotent-by-client-supplied-ID in that sense, though not a pure no-op retry (a second call with the same ID is rejected, not silently accepted). If this is the first unit ever enqueued against the path, a `WorkPool` is auto-provisioned as release-fed with a default WIP limit. Publishes `WorkUnitCreated`.
A unit becomes a pack-aware pick (`workKind` `CASE_PICK` / `EACH_PICK`) when the body carries `quantity` (eaches), `pickUnit` or `fromBin`, or a `BREAK_CASE` when it carries `caseBreak` (ADR-0045); both need a `sku` and the two never mix. A `CASE` pick needs an active CASE pack level in the local copy and a whole number of cases.

**Idempotency (ADR-0022, replay classes ADR-0050).** This resource-creating POST requires a caller-supplied `Idempotency-Key` header. The first request with a given key is processed and its final response (status, headers, body) is stored in the same database transaction as the write; a retry with the same key and the same body replays that stored response verbatim and does not enqueue again. A refusal is stored only when it is final for the request — a validation of the request's own fields (FINAL). A refusal that depends on state that can change (`unknown-path-id`, `wip-limit-reached`, `no-active-case-level`, `quantity-not-case-multiple`, any 5xx) is not stored: the key is released, so the same key can be retried and executes again (a different body under it is a new request, not `idempotency-key-reused`). A missing key is `400 idempotency-key-required`; the same key with a different body after a stored answer is `409 idempotency-key-reused`. Use a fresh key per logical action. A replay carries `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.
Superseded by the K1 choreography (X3): order-management publishes `OrderAllocated` / `OrderPartiallyAllocated` and this service's `ApplyOrderAllocated` consumer enqueues one work unit per line (OM ADR 0005 / WP ADR-0031); removal planned with the next breaking window.

  parameters={[{"name":"pathId","in":"path","required":true,"description":"The process path's identifier — a named station that owns a queue (unit-in → unit-out), e.g. a pick zone or pack line. The write endpoints (enqueueWorkUnit, configurePool) reject ids outside the declared families with `400 unknown-path-id`; read endpoints surface a missing pool/projection as `404` instead.\n","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"pattern":"^(pick|pack|rebin|slam)(-.*)?$"},"example":"pick-a"},{"name":"Idempotency-Key","in":"header","required":true,"description":"Caller-supplied key that makes a retried POST safe (ADR-0022, ADR-0047). 1-128 printable ASCII characters; **clients must always send one** (missing: `400 idempotency-key-required`; malformed: `400 idempotency-key-invalid`). Generate a fresh UUID per logical submit and reuse it only to retry that same request. The key is global: reusing it with a different method, path or body is `409 idempotency-key-reused`. A replayed answer carries `Idempotency-Replayed: true`.\n","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128},"example":"6f1c9a52-8f6e-4a0b-9d44-2c1b0f7a3e55"}]}
